summary: David P. Chandler works in history and archaeology. He studied at Harvard College, Harvard University, Yale, and the University of Michigan, and held posts at Monash University (~1972–1997), Johns Hopkins, Cornell, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison.

David P. Jackson is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Southampton and the University of Washington under David Seyfort Ruegg, he served as a C-3 professor at the University of Hamburg (1992–2007).

David Patt is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundup Sopa (attested 1993) and also studied under Lobsang Tenzin and Geshe Thubten Tandhar.

David Phillip Stanley specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins and David Germano, later serving at Naropa University and as Co-Director of the Nitartha Institute (attested 2019).

David Pingree specialized in Indology and the history of archaeology. Educated at Harvard under Otto E. Neugebauer and Daniel H. H. Ingalls, he held posts at the University of Chicago (1963–1971) and Brown University (from 1971).

David R. Kinsley was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at Drew University, Union Theological Seminary, and the University of Chicago (PhD ~1964–1970), and served as department chair at McMaster University (1969–2000).

David R. Loy works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Carleton College, King's College London, the University of Hawaiʻi, and the National University of Singapore, holding posts at Bunkyo University (1990–2006) and Xavier University (~2006–2010).

David Ralph Quinter specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned his PhD at Stanford under Carl Bielefeldt and Bernard Faure, and held positions at Indiana University Bloomington, Washington University in St. Louis, and the University of Alberta (from 2008).
David Reigle works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and was affiliated with the Asian Humanities Press (attested 2006).

David Roy Shackleton Bailey was a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Cambridge, he taught there (1948–1968), at the University of Michigan (1968–1974, 1988–2002), and as Pope Professor at Harvard (1975–1988).
David Ruddell was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Laval University and served as Secretary at Fort William College.

David Schaberg is a sinologist who studied at Stanford University and Harvard University (PhD ~1989–1996). Since 1996, he has held academic posts at the University of California, Los Angeles, becoming Dean of Humanities in 2012.

David Seyfort Ruegg was a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and held posts at Leiden University (1966–1972), the University of Hamburg (1983–1990), and SOAS (~1985–1996).

David Shea worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Indology. He studied at Trinity College Dublin (1793–1798) and served as an Assistant Professor at the East India Company College (1826–1836).

David Slakter specializes in Indology and philosophy. He earned a master's degree from the University of Liverpool under Christopher Bartley (2007–2012) and became an assistant professor at Camden County College in 2024.
David Steindl-Rast is a scholar in religious studies. He completed his studies at the University of Vienna (~1945–1952) and the Academy of Fine Arts Vienna.

David Teplitz was an Indology scholar who earned an MA from Northwestern University and a PhD from the American Academy of Asian Studies. He held a teaching post at the California Institute of Integral Studies.

David Tracy is a religious studies and philosophy scholar. He studied at St. Joseph's Seminary and the Pontifical Gregorian University, later teaching at the Catholic University of America (1967–1969) and the University of Chicago (1969–2006).

David W. Chappell was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at Mount Allison, McGill, and Yale, he was a professor at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1971–2000) and later taught at Soka University of America.

David W. Tien works in sinology and philosophy. He studied at McGill University, the University of Toronto, and the University of Michigan, where he earned his PhD under doctoral supervisor James Robson (attested 2009).
